text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - German Bund futures skidded lower in late trade, for the second session in a row, a wave of selling overcoming technical supports. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.74, down 0/49 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts sank to a two-week low after an auction of stock due 2021 attracted cover of just 1.29 times with a lengthy yield tail. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 111-31/32, down 31/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Ten-year bond futures slid in concert with Bunds to settle at the day's lows. Sentiment was undermined by weaker U.S. Treasuries ahead of Memorial Day weekend, while PIBOR was also weak. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.82, down 0.76 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets remained weak, pulled down by Bunds despite underlying positive current in Btps. There was some near term disappointment that the Bank of Italy did not cut rates after preliminary May CPI data. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.48, down 0.97 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries weakened at the long end in mid-morning trade althought the pre-Memorial Day weekend activity was thin. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-03/32, down 06/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.99 percent.

JAPAN - Key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures rebounded by the close after Wednesday's sell-off on a report that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) was considering the timing for a credit tightening. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 123.89, up 0.10 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market was fairly quiet with just a handful of small, retail-targeted deals to keep syndicate desks ticking over. British Land's 300 million sterling convertible bond, launched on Tuesday, rallied to 104.50 bid on broker screens, giving a paper profit of 7.0 percentage points, or just over 20 million pounds for those involved in the deal.
